characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: EMPYREAN, PANALYTICAL, Co-Kα source (40 kV, 40 mA), scan rate 5° min−1
characterization_methods.key_findings: BCC (ferrite) major phase (56.00%) + partially ordered B2 (34.00%) + trace γ-brass type (1.60%) + Fe5Si3-type silicide (8.40%); refinement wR = 3.326, GoF = 1.33, χ² = 1.78; crystallite sizes BCC 29 nm, B2 27 nm, γ-brass 21 nm, Fe5Si3 23 nm
characterization_methods.purpose: Phase identification, phase fraction, lattice parameter, crystallite size and microstrain of the SPSed sample
characterization_methods.technique: High-resolution X-ray diffraction (XRD) with Rietveld refinement (GSAS-II)

characterization_methods.key_findings: Multiple contrasts (white, black, light grey, dark grey) corresponding to BCC, B2 type, γ-brass type and Fe5Si3-type intermetallic phases; dark agglomerated features show onion-type layered appearance
characterization_methods.purpose: Microstructural feature imaging of the SPSed pellet

characterization_methods.key_findings: Presence of all constituent elements (Fe, Mn, Ni, Al, Si, C) confirms chemical homogeneity of the SPSed pellet at the full-area scale
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: full-area analysis of the SPSed pellet
characterization_methods.purpose: Elemental analysis of the SPSed sample

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: CAMECA SXFive; WDS, LaB6 filament, TAP/PET/LIF/LPET/LTAP crystals; 15 kV, 10 nA; carbon-coated 20 nm
characterization_methods.key_findings: White contrast rich in Al and Ni (spot 1) = B2-type phase; light grey contrast rich in Fe, Mn and Ni (spot 2) = BCC ferritic phase; Fe, Mn, Ni almost uniform, Al segregated (B2 network), Si locally enriched (Fe5Si3); γ-brass regions hard to distinguish due to very low fraction. Spot 1: Fe 32.46, Mn 10.00, Ni 32.09, Al 21.82, Si 2.63 wt.%; Spot 2: Fe 44.53, Mn 21.60, Ni 20.66, Al 7.33, Si 5.88 wt.%.
characterization_methods.purpose: Identify phase chemistry and elemental distribution in the SPSed sample
characterization_methods.technique: Electron probe micro analyzer (BSE imaging, quantitative point WDS analysis, X-ray elemental mapping)

characterization_methods.key_findings: Microhardness 7.8 ± 0.3 GPa; elastic modulus 184 ± 5 GPa; indentation depth ~5.08 μm; no crack formation even at 5000 mN
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: 5000 mN load, dwell 20 s, approach speed 80 μm/min, retract speed 16 μm/min, loading/unloading rate 10,000 mN/min; at least six measurements
characterization_methods.purpose: Measure microhardness and elastic modulus of the SPSed pellet

characterization_methods.key_findings: Average ultimate compressive stress 2046 ± 160 MPa with ~19% compressive strain
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: 25 °C, specimen diameter 4 mm × height 8 mm (ratio 1:2), crosshead speed 0.5 mm/min, strain rate 10^-3 s−1; repeated three times
characterization_methods.purpose: Evaluate compressive strength and ductility of the SPSed sample

computational_details.boundary_and_initial_conditions: Pressure = 100000.0 Pa; system size = 1.0 mol; mole fraction Mn = 0.19, Ni = 0.15, Al = 0.15, Si = 0.1, C = 0.01
computational_details.simulation_method: CALPHAD thermodynamic modelling (property diagram and single-point equilibrium)
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: Predicted phases (BCC/B2/γ-brass/silicide) were correlated with the experimentally observed phases; some differences were attributed to using the TCFE8 database instead of TCHEA3.

analytical_models.model_note: Δσ_gb evaluated as 1085 MPa (BCC) and 1224 MPa (B2-type).
Dispersion strengthening of the BCC phase: 54 MPa (silicide) and 111 MPa (B2-type); for B2-type phase 55 MPa (silicide).
Δσ_ss = 106 MPa (BCC) and 177 MPa (B2-type); Al taken as solute for both phases.

computational_details.boundary_and_initial_conditions: Assumed phase fractions of BCC and B2-type for the strengthening calculation taken as 62.0% and 38.0% respectively (from measured 56.0% BCC and 34.0% B2).
computational_details.simulation_method: Analytical strengthening-mechanism modelling of yield strength
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: Total calculated theoretical strength 2164 MPa vs measured 2046 ± 160 MPa; grain boundary (52.55%) and dislocation (30.00%) strengthening are the dominant mechanisms.

interfaces.interface_notes: SEM/BSE contrast classes: white = B2 (rich in Al and Ni), light grey = BCC (rich in Fe, Mn, Ni), dark grey/black = γ-brass type and Fe5Si3-type intermetallic; dark features show an onion-type layered appearance. Regions of γ-brass type are difficult to distinguish by EPMA due to its very low phase fraction.
interfaces.phase_evolution: The BCC and partially ordered B2-type phases were retained after spark plasma sintering along with the in-situ formation of the Fe5Si3-type silicide phase; γ-brass type survives only as a trace. Retention of BCC and B2 is attributed to strong Fe–Al and Ni–Al bonding and the sluggish diffusion effect in the high entropy steel; silicide formation results from undissolved Si remaining after milling and the strongly negative Fe–Si and Mn–Si binary mixing enthalpies.

comparative_performance.comparison_metric: Microhardness vs density and ultimate compressive strength vs density compared with conventional stainless steel, dual-phase steel, low-density steel and other HEAs (Fig. 9(e,f); Supplementary Table S1); ferritic dual-phase steel microhardness is 2.0–2.4 GPa while the present alloy is 7.8 GPa.

processing_steps.atmosphere: toluene (process control reagent to avoid oxidation)
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Elemental powders Fe, Ni, Mn, Al, Si, C (99.2% pure) in proportion Fe40Mn19Ni15Al15Si10C1 (at.%) milled in planetary ball mill (Retsch PM 400/2) at 200 rpm; ball-to-powder ratio 10:1; WC vials and WC balls; milling stopped intermittently for 20 min after every 1 h to avoid overheating; powder sampled every 5 h.

35 h milled powder consolidated by SPS (Dr. Sinter SCM 1050, Japan) at 900 °C, pressure of 50 MPa, heating rate 100 °C.min−1, holding time 15 min; SPSed pellet diameter ~30 mm and thickness ~9 mm; graphite layer removed by polishing; relative density ~99%.

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Microhardness: MHT3 Anton Paar instrumented tester, 5000 mN load, dwell time 20 s, approach speed 80 μm/min, retract speed 16 μm/min, loading and unloading rate 10,000 mN/min, Vickers diamond indenter, at least six measurements; elastic modulus and hardness from Oliver-Pharr method. Compression: Instron 5982 100 kN UTM, crosshead speed 0.5 mm/min, test repeated three times.

tensile_properties.stress_strain_curves: Compressive engineering stress-strain curve (Fig. 9(c)) rising monotonically to ~2046 MPa at ~0.19 strain

phases_present.morphology: light grey contrast matrix (Fe, Mn, Ni-rich)
white contrast (rich in Al and Ni)

structures.overall_structure: Multi-phase structure with BCC (ferrite) as the major phase, partially ordered B2 as secondary phase, plus a trace amount of γ-brass type phase and a Fe5Si3-type silicide phase; nanocrystalline features retained after SPS.

unmapped_findings: Theoretical density of the alloy computed by rule of mixture is 6.55 g/cc; the SPSed pellet shows a relative density of ~99% (ρRD = ρexp/ρth × 100).
Melting point of the high entropy steel calculated via a machine-learning approach is 1638 K and via the rule of mixture is 1620 K.

Strengthening-mechanism contribution fractions for the SPSed sample: grain boundary 52.55%, dislocation 30.00%, precipitation 5.70%, solid solution 6.14%; grain-boundary and dislocation strengthening are the dominant mechanisms.
Sum of calculated theoretical strengthening contributions is 2164 MPa, in close agreement with the measured strength of 2046 MPa (Table 9; B2-type column).
Indentation depth of the SPSed sample was ~5.08 μm, and the optical micrograph of the indent showed no evidence of crack formation even at a load of 5000 mN.

Thermodynamic parameters of the non-equiatomic FeMnNiAlSiC HES: ΔH_mix = −8.4 kJ/mol, ΔS_conf = 12.4 J/K·mol, δ = 7.6 %, Ω = 2.4, VEC = 6.9; VEC lies in the 6.87 < VEC < 8.0 (BCC + FCC) band while δ exceeds the δ ≤ 6.6 limit.
